evals.prompt: The pinned deep-reviewer's checklist reports a `blocker`-severity finding during a run.
evals.expected_output: A blocker-severity finding always maps to P1: severity determines the filed issue's priority prefix directly.

evals.prompt: The diff between the checkpoint commit and the current default-branch tip is empty -- nothing merged since the last run.
evals.expected_output: Report that there is nothing new since the checkpoint and stop: no dispatch, no checkpoint update -- advancing the checkpoint on an empty diff would be a no-op that only obscures the last real review.

evals.prompt: A candidate finding has concrete file:line evidence, but the dedup pass (which searches `--state all`, so a closed issue counts as tracked too) finds an existing `ultra-review`-labeled issue already tracking the same file and description.
evals.expected_output: Skip filing: a finding the dedup pass confirms is already tracked is never re-filed, even though it independently satisfies the file:line evidence bar on its own.

evals.prompt: 27 candidate issues survive the dedup pass in a single run.
evals.expected_output: When more than roughly 15 candidate issues survive dedup in one run, stop short of filing any of them and report the batch for a human to look at, rather than auto-filing a flood.

evals.prompt: A fresh re-read of the checkpoint issue immediately before writing shows a different `Last reviewed commit` than the sha this run read back in step 2 -- a concurrent run already advanced the checkpoint while this run was in flight.
evals.expected_output: Because the reviewed ranges may overlap in that case, this run does not write the checkpoint at all -- the Cumulative counters take a permanent undercount for this run's own contribution instead of a retry.

evals.prompt: A filed finding's blamed commit carries zero Co-Authored-By trailers, and a second filed finding's blamed commit carries two distinct Co-Authored-By trailers naming different collaborators.
evals.expected_output: The first finding is bucketed as unattributed (no trailer to attribute to, and the commit's own author is never used as a fallback); the second is bucketed as ambiguous (two distinct names, never guess between them).
